title: Einstein Writes to Marie Curie
text:
In the autumn of 1911 Marie Curie was the most famous woman scientist in the world. In early November she attended the first Solvay Conference in Brussels with Albert Einstein and other leading physicists. While she was there, the Paris press broke the story of her relationship with the physicist Paul Langevin, who was married. Newspapers attacked her as a foreign homewrecker, crowds gathered outside her house, and the scandal turned ugly.

In the middle of it she learned she had won her second Nobel Prize, in chemistry. A member of the Swedish Academy wrote suggesting she stay away from the ceremony.

On November 23, 1911, Einstein, who had admired her mind and character at the conference, wrote her a short letter. He told her he was angry at the base way the public was dealing with her, and urged her simply not to read the trash being written about her, but to leave it to the people it was made for. He added that he and others were grateful to have people like her among them.

Curie went to Stockholm in December and accepted the prize in person.
lesson: A word of support to someone being publicly humiliated means more than any praise in good times. Write it, even if you think you have nothing important to say.
source: Albert Einstein, letter to Marie Curie, November 23, 1911, The Collected Papers of Albert Einstein, vol. 8
